Comments, Suggestions, and Version History

Review documents with your team: comment, reply, and assign tasks, suggest edits instead of making them, accept or reject suggestions, and name and restore versions.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Add a comment, reply to one, and resolve it
  • ✓Assign a comment to a person with an @mention
  • ✓Switch to Suggesting mode, suggest an edit, and accept or reject suggestions
  • ✓Open version history, name the current version, and restore an earlier one

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Comments

On the job

You own the draft of Parkview's new pet policy.

Denise and Marcus have read the draft. Denise left a comment, Marcus suggested two changes, and Priya still needs to confirm the monthly pet fee. You need to work through the feedback without losing track of the original wording.

Your task: Handle comments and suggestions, assign the open question, and mark the reviewed version.

  • Select the text, then click Add comment on the toolbar, choose Insert › Comment, or press Ctrl+Alt+M. Type the comment and click Comment.
  • Comments show in the right margin, attached to the text. Click one to reply.
  • When a comment is handled, click Resolve (the check mark in the top corner of the comment) to close it. To see closed comments again, click Comments at the top right; Re-open brings one back.
  • To assign a comment, type @ and the person's name in it, check Assign to, and click Assign. The person is notified and is responsible for marking it done.

Suggesting mode

In Suggesting mode, your edits do not change the text. They appear as colored suggestions with your name, and the document's editors accept or reject each one. It is the Google Docs version of Word's Track Changes.

  • Switch modes with the mode button at the right end of the toolbar (it shows Editing): choose Suggesting. Or use View › Mode › Suggesting, or press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+X.
  • Type, delete, or replace text as usual. Each change becomes a suggestion card in the margin.
  • To accept or reject one, click the check mark or the X on its card. Tools › Review suggested edits shows them all, with Accept all and Reject all.
  • Viewing mode shows the document without suggestions or comments, as it would print.

Version history

  • Open it with the Last edit (clock) icon at the top right, File › Version history › See version history, or Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H.
  • Click a version on the right to see what it looked like and who changed what.
  • Restore: choose the earlier version, click Restore this version at the top, then click Restore. The file goes back to the way it was in that version.
  • Name a version to find it later: File › Version history › Name current version, or in the list, choose More › Name this version. A document can have up to 40 named versions.
  • Only people who can edit the file can see its version history.
Worked example

Marking the reviewed pet policy

The team has reviewed the draft, and you expect more changes later.

  1. 1

    Accept and reject the suggestions, and resolve the comments that are handled.

    The margin should show only what is still open.

  2. 2

    File › Version history › Name current version: Reviewed by office.

    If later edits go wrong, you can find and restore this exact version by name.

Result: A clean draft, plus a named version to return to.

🔑 Name a version at every milestone: first draft, reviewed, final.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Review a document with a classmate or a second account of your own.

  1. Share a practice document with your partner as a Commenter.
  2. Ask them to add a comment and to suggest one change in Suggesting mode.
  3. Reply to the comment and resolve it. Accept or reject the suggestion.
  4. Name the current version Reviewed. Then make an edit and restore the Reviewed version from version history.
Deliverable: Submit a screenshot of version history showing your named version to your instructor or course folder. No partner? Complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
